You, Me and Namyangju당신과 나 남양주에서

“You, Me and Namyangju” places an uncertain encounter in the snow beside a fox’s account of its present life. The speaker watches someone move away, while the ending leaves room for both contentment and thoughts of someone absent.

BACKGROUND

A little background

Danpyunsun’s release notes date the first draft to 2022, a revision to 2023 and completion to 2025. He says the song felt too light for Hail to the Music; when returning to it, he kept thinking of images from 1980s and 1990s Hong Kong films, without identifying exactly how they shaped the song.

INSIDE THE LYRICS

A present life with room for memory

  • Uncertain closeness
  • Separation
  • Contentment and memory

Snow and visible breath give the encounter physical details, yet the speaker questions whether their being together is real. Repeated attention to the other person’s appearance and footsteps keeps returning to the same movement: someone is getting farther away. The lyric offers no settled explanation of what happened between them.

The spoken ending shifts to a figure who says they have become a fox. Cold weather and searching the snow for insects make this new life concrete, even within its strange premise. The figure expresses satisfaction with the present, then repeatedly admits to thinking of the other person sometimes. Remembering them does not cancel that satisfaction; both feelings remain.

ABOUT THE ARTIST / 단편선 순간들

Danpyunsun and the Moments Ensemble

Danpyunsun and the Moments Ensemble brings songwriter and producer Danpyunsun together with players on piano, bass, drums and guitar. In his notes for Hail to the Music, he describes making music around the ways people watch, feel and respond to one another.

The ensemble announced its beginning in January 2024. Its lineup that year included pianist Lee Boram, bassist Song Hyunwoo, drummer Park Jaejun and guitarist Park Jangmi alongside Danpyunsun.
